rationale: F16 (vue final review 2026-09-30): `defineOptions({ name: 'X' })` — the `<script setup>` way to declare a component's name — was never read for its `name`. The macro appeared in VUE_COMPILER_MACROS only so that its CALL edge would be filtered, and nothing else looked inside it, so a component written the modern way fell back to the FILE STEM. Found by the contains oracle disagreeing in a direction that pointed at the ANALYZER rather than the oracle. Two corpus cases: table/src/table-body/td-wrapper.vue declares `name: 'TableTdWrapper'` and was published as `td-wrapper`; splitter/src/split-bar.vue declares `name: 'ElSplitterBar'` and was published as `split-bar`. The consequence is not cosmetic — every component-owned edge sources the identity and the store's symbol key is name+line, so the declared name and the published one are two different symbols and a query for the declared name finds nothing. The `size` prop is declared with the inline generic form so the fixture also proves the macro rename RE-POINTSED ownership rather than orphaning the component's own members, which is the failure mode a rename without a re-point would produce.

forbidSymbols.name: define-options-name
forbidSymbols.note: the file stem must not remain the identity when defineOptions declares one
